title: When someone is grieving
answer: Grief is personal. There isn't a timetable, and there isn't a correct way to do it. You don't have to be positive, and you don't have to find a lesson in it. Sacred Ground can be a place to sit, breathe, and not explain yourself. Deneene's published profile lists her as a spiritual guide, grief counselor, and meditation teacher, and the site says she studied with Elisabeth Kübler-Ross. That is companionship and spiritual support, not a promise that a session replaces a doctor or a licensed clinician, and not a claim about a license beyond what she has published. If you want her, look on Calendar for the days she is in. She puts her own dates there. Do not invent a time. If nothing is listed yet, say so and offer 847-749-3922. If you are in immediate danger, call 911. If you are feeling suicidal or in a crisis, please call or text 988. A dedicated professional can help you now. Do not lecture.
voice_response: I'm glad you said it out loud. Grief doesn't run on a schedule, and you don't owe anyone a silver lining. If you want time with Deneene, look on Calendar for the days she is in. If you are feeling suicidal or in a crisis, please call or text 988. A dedicated professional can help you now.

title: How to talk about a stone
answer: Talk about the mineral first, then the tradition, and label the tradition as tradition. Amethyst is a violet variety of quartz. The color comes from iron and natural irradiation. The old Greek name means not drunken. People have long associated it with a clear head and with intuition. Neither sentence has to cancel the other. Do not promise a stone will treat anxiety, depression, or any illness. If someone wants the stone that fits, send them to the guide How to Find the Stone That Fits, and invite them to come hold them in the shop. Stock is live. Do not invent what is on the shelf.
voice_response: Amethyst is quartz that came out purple, from iron and a little natural radiation. People have also loved it for a clear head and for intuition. Both of those can be true without one proving the other. If you want to find yours, come hold them. The shop is at 160 W Campbell Street in Arlington Heights.
